tone_statements.citation: Kamanda Kola, Roger. 1989. La conjugaison en ngbandi (langue non bantu). Annales Aequatoria 10: 181-199 (+ tableau de conjugaison).
tone_statements.quote: Le ngbandi distingue trois tonèmes simples et deux tonèmes complexes. a. Tonèmes simples : - bas : ya "épouse" - moyen : y... "ventre" - haut : y... "vent" b. Tonèmes complexes : descendant - haut-bas ... "canard", - haut-moyen ... "depuis longtemps" - montant : - bas-haut : lu "chatine", - bas-moyen d... "hache" ... Le nombre de syllabe dans un mot est déterminé par le nombre de tons portés par ce mot. ... [RESUME, p. 181:] la conjugaison, laquelle connaît trois valeurs tonales (le haut, le bas, et le moyen).
tone_statements.translation: Ngbandi distinguishes three simple tonemes and two complex tonemes. a. Simple tonemes: low ya 'wife', mid y.. 'belly', high y.. 'wind'. b. Complex tonemes: falling - high-low .. 'duck', high-mid .. 'for a long time'; rising - low-high lu .., low-mid d.. 'axe' ... The number of syllables in a word is determined by the number of tones the word carries. ... [Abstract:] the conjugation, which has three tonal values (high, low and mid).
tone_statements.locator: Annales Aequatoria 10 (1989), pp. 183-184, sect. 1.2 'Phonemes suprasegmentaux' / 1.2.1 'Tonemes' and p. 184 sect. 1.3 'Syllabe'; abstract p. 181; verb tone classes pp. 185-186, morphotonologie verbale pp. 186ff
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Three level tonemes (low, mid, high) plus falling (H-L, H-M) and rising (L-H, L-M) contours, the falling tone said to be rare; every vowel/syllable bears a tone (syllable count = tone count); verb lexemes have underlying stable tones plus possibly a floating low tone, grouped in four tone classes; tense/mood expressed by tonomorphemes (mid = present, high = past, mid = future) realised as tonal a…

(2) Deciding source: a first-hand descriptive work by the language's principal linguist (Boyeldieu, SELAF 1975), but only the 10-page phonological-revision chapter, reached through an unattributed Rosetta excerpt; the attribution to Boyeldieu 1975 was independently verified against the source via Glottolog refs and the 1979 Persée review. It is not the best available description: Boyeldieu 1973 (primary phonology, 60 pp) and Maba 2020 (378-pp PhD grammar with phonology) exist and are not yet obtained; neither has an open copy (HAL, DiCAMES, archive.org, LLACAN checked; (3) downloaded now: Boyeldieu 2013

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2013. Logophorique et discours rapporté en yakoma. In P. Boyeldieu (ed.), Logophorique et discours rapporté en Afrique centrale, 187-213. Louvain-Paris: Peeters. (HAL halshs-00658413)
sources.quote: 'La langue oppose trois hauteurs tonales distinctives, B (à), M (å) et H (á) et connaît plusieurs modulations lexicales, en particulier HB (â) et BM (à¯).' Verb mood (réel/virtuel/nécessaire) and verb number are expressed by tonal identity of the index-verb pair. No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the paper.

sources.quote: Mode and verb number marked by 'variation tonale' / 'identité tonale' (citing Boyeldieu 1995); plural verb 'à ton haut (dú vs dù)'. Silent on stress/accent.

sources.note: Phonology sketch gives three simple tonemes (bas, moyen, haut) and two complex tonemes (descendant H-L / H-M, montant L-H / L-M); syllable count = tone count; verbs carry a 'tonomorpheme', lexemes fall into four tone classes (I low, II mid, IIIa/IIIb high, IIIb with a final floating low, IV high..low); TAM (present = mid tonomorpheme, past = high, future = mid) marked by tonal variation on verb lexemes and subject substitutes; 'dureme'/intoneme for emphasis and questions. No stress statement.
